docs.title: MSFLib Account Module
docs.text: The Account module provides account and profile domain APIs for MSFLib-based applications.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This module handles user account management including registration, authentication, profile management, and administrative account operations.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Account self endpoints (/account) for authenticated users
  • Optional open registration endpoint with configurable path (POST /account/open by default)
  • Admin account management endpoints (/admin/accounts)
  • Profile endpoints (/profiles) including avatar upload
  • Optional nested profile creation during account registration
  • Action classes for account and profile business logic

docs.title: For Pydantic v2 (recommended):
docs.text:
[tool.poetry.dependencies]
msflib = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "core", rev = "dev" }
msflib-account = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "modules/account", rev = "dev" }

docs.title: For Pydantic v1 (legacy):
docs.text:
[tool.poetry.dependencies]
pydantic = "^1.10"
pydantic-settings = "^1.10"

msflib = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "core", rev = "core-v0.1.1" }
msflib-account = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "modules/account", rev = "account-v0.1.0" }

See Pydantic Version Compatibility for migration guidance.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
from fastapi import FastAPI
from msflib.account.router import account_router, account_admin_router, profile_router

app = FastAPI()

app.include_router(
    account_router(
        get_session=get_session,
        get_current_account=get_current_account,
        settings=settings,
        account_type=Account,
        profile_type=Profile,
    )
)

app.include_router(
    account_admin_router(
        get_session=get_session,
        role_check=role_check,
        settings=settings,
        account_type=Account,
        profile_type=Profile,
    )
)

app.include_router(
    profile_router(
        get_session=get_session,
        get_current_account=get_current_account,
        get_current_active_account=get_current_active_account,
        settings=settings,
        account_type=Account,
        profile_type=Profile,
    )
)

If ACCOUNT.USERS_OPEN_REGISTRATION is enabled, the account router exposes exactly one open signup route. By default that route is /account/open, but you can override it with either open_registration_path= when building the router or ACCOUNT.OPEN_REGISTRATION_PATH in settings.

docs.title: Account (/account)
docs.text:
• GET /me - current authenticated account
  • POST /open - open registration on a single configurable route (when enabled)
  • PUT /me - update current account
  • POST /verify-availability - check email/username/phone availability

docs.title: Admin Accounts (/admin/accounts)
docs.text:
• GET / - list accounts (admin)
  • POST / - create account (admin)
  • PUT /{account_id} - update account (admin)
  • GET /{account_id} - read account (admin)

docs.title: Profiles (/profiles)
docs.text:
• GET / - current account profile
  • GET /{account_id} - account profile by account id
  • POST / - create or update current profile
  • PUT / - update current profile
  • PUT /avatar - upload current profile avatar
  • PUT /{id} - update profile by profile id

docs.title: Actions
docs.text:
• AccountAction - Handles account CRUD operations and business logic
  • ProfileAction - Handles profile CRUD operations and business logic

docs.title: Models
docs.text:
• AccountBase - Base account model
  • AccountCreate - Schema for account creation
  • AccountUpdate - Schema for account updates
  • AccountRead - Schema for account responses
  • ProfileBase - Base profile model
  • ProfileCreate - Schema for profile creation
  • ProfileUpdate - Schema for profile updates
  • ProfileRead - Schema for profile responses

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Account-specific settings are accessed via settings.scope("ACCOUNT") and include: - USERS_OPEN_REGISTRATION - Enable/disable open registration - OPEN_REGISTRATION_PATH - Custom path for open registration endpoint - Other account-related configuration options

docs.title: Creating an Account (Open Registration)
docs.text:
When open registration is enabled, users can create accounts without authentication:

POST /account/open
{
    "email": "user@example.com",
    "username": "username",
    "password": "securepassword"
}

docs.title: Getting Current Account
docs.text:
Authenticated users can retrieve their own account information:

GET /account/me
Authorization: Bearer <token>

docs.title: Updating Account
docs.text:
Users can update their own account information:

PUT /account/me
Authorization: Bearer <token>
{
    "email": "newemail@example.com",
    "current_password": "oldpassword",
    "new_password": "newpassword"
}

docs.title: Admin Account Management
docs.text:
Administrators can manage all accounts:

GET /admin/accounts
Authorization: Bearer <admin-token>

docs.title: Events
docs.text: The account module emits several events that can be hooked into: - account-created - After an account is created - account-pre-update - Before an account is updated - account-updated - After an account is updated - Similar events exist for profile operations

docs.title: MSFLib AI Core Module
docs.text: msflib-ai-core provides the infrastructure layer for AI features in MSFLib. It contains provider-agnostic factories for chat models, embeddings, vector stores, and request-level usage/rate-limit helpers.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This module intentionally has no API router and no domain actions. It is designed to be a foundational layer for AI capabilities in MSFLib-based applications.

docs.title: Capabilities
docs.text:
• Unified LLM factory (get_llm) across OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure, Ollama, Bedrock
  • Unified embeddings factory (get_embeddings)
  • Vector store backend dispatch (get_vector_store) for pgvector and future backends
  • Token usage callback for LangChain runs
  • Redis-based request-per-minute limiter
  • LangGraph checkpointer factory with tenant/workspace checkpoint scoping policy and managed context lifecycle
  • LangGraph long-term memory store factory with tenant/workspace namespace policy and managed context lifecycle
  • Dependency namespace helpers for easy FastAPI integration

docs.title: Developer Guide Coverage
docs.text:
This documentation is a practical integration guide for downstream applications. It covers:

  1. Runtime policy mapping from resolved settings (LangChainConfigBridge)
  2. Prompt name mapping and context source ordering
  3. Provider-first chunking and ingestion pipeline usage (IngestionPipeline)
  4. Scoped checkpoint utilities (CheckpointScope) and checkpointer factory
  5. Scoped long-term memory utilities (MemoryStoreScope) and store factory
  6. Memory lifecycle event hooks via eventbus (emit_if_listeners)
  7. Retrieval scoping helpers with mandatory tenant/workspace filters (similarity_search_scoped)

If you are integrating ai_core into a consuming app, start with the examples in:

  1. Downstream Usage Examples
  2. Usage

docs.title: Dependency Notes
docs.text:
• langgraph is a direct dependency for checkpoint and long-term memory store integration in ai_core.
  • Postgres checkpointing is optional and enabled by the Poetry extra checkpoint-postgres (langgraph-checkpoint-postgres).
  • Postgres long-term memory store uses the same optional package, langgraph-checkpoint-postgres, enabled via the checkpoint-postgres extra.

docs.title: LangGraph Managed Factories
docs.text:
create_langgraph_checkpointer(...) and create_langgraph_store(...) return managed context managers by design.

  • Sync usage: with ... as resource
  • Async usage: async with ... as resource when async_mode=True

Postgres setup behavior:

  • run_setup defaults to False for both factories.
  • This avoids running database setup DDL on every context entry (for example, once per request in FastAPI).
  • Run setup once during app startup by passing run_setup=True in startup initialization code, then keep request-path usage at the default False.

Example (sync):

from msflib.ai_core.services.checkpoint_policy import create_langgraph_checkpointer
from msflib.ai_core.services.memory_store_policy import create_langgraph_store

with create_langgraph_checkpointer(backend="memory") as checkpointer:
    # pass checkpointer into LangGraph compile(...)
    ...

with create_langgraph_store(backend="memory") as store:
    store.put(("tenant", "t1", "workspace", "w1", "memories", "semantic"), "k", {"v": 1})

Example (async):

from msflib.ai_core.services.checkpoint_policy import create_langgraph_checkpointer
from msflib.ai_core.services.memory_store_policy import create_langgraph_store

async with create_langgraph_checkpointer(backend="postgres", connection_string=dsn, async_mode=True) as checkpointer:
    ...

async with create_langgraph_store(backend="postgres", connection_string=dsn, async_mode=True) as store:
    ...

Startup initialization example (postgres):

from msflib.ai_core.services.checkpoint_policy import create_langgraph_checkpointer
from msflib.ai_core.services.memory_store_policy import create_langgraph_store


def initialize_langgraph_postgres_resources(dsn: str) -> None:
    with create_langgraph_checkpointer(
        backend="postgres",
        connection_string=dsn,
        run_setup=True,
    ) as checkpointer:
        # No need to do anything, the context manager runs the setup.
        pass

    with create_langgraph_store(
        backend="postgres",
        connection_string=dsn,
        run_setup=True,
    ) as store:
        # No need to do anything, the context manager runs the setup.
        pass

from msflib.ai_core.services.ingestion_pipeline import IngestionPipeline

docs.title: Scoped Memory Store
docs.text:
from msflib.ai_core.services.memory_store_policy import create_langgraph_store

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: AI Core settings are accessed via settings.scope("AI_CORE") and include:

docs.title: LLM Settings
docs.text:
• LLM_PROVIDER - One of: openai, anthropic, azure, ollama, bedrock, openrouter, groq
  • LLM_MODEL - Model identifier (e.g., "gpt-4o")
  • LLM_API_KEY - API key for the provider
  • LLM_BASE_URL - Custom base URL (for Azure, Ollama, etc.)
  • LLM_TEMPERATURE - Sampling temperature (0.0 to 2.0)
  • LLM_MAX_TOKENS - Maximum tokens to generate

docs.title: Embedding Settings
docs.text:
• EMBEDDING_PROVIDER - One of: openai, azure, ollama, bedrock
  • EMBEDDING_MODEL - Embedding model identifier
  • EMBEDDING_API_KEY - API key for the provider
  • EMBEDDING_BASE_URL - Custom base URL

docs.title: Vector Store Settings
docs.text:
• VECTOR_STORE_BACKEND - Currently only pgvector
  • VECTOR_STORE_URL - Connection string for PostgreSQL
  • VECTOR_STORE_API_KEY - API key (if required by the backend)
  • VECTOR_STORE_COLLECTION_PREFIX - Prefix for collection names

docs.title: Rate Limiting and Budgets
docs.text:
• RATE_LIMIT_RPM - Requests per minute limit
  • TOKEN_BUDGET_PER_WORKSPACE - Maximum tokens per workspace (optional)

docs.title: Policies
docs.text:
• MIDDLEWARE_POLICY - Configuration for AI middleware (see MiddlewarePolicySchema)
  • CHUNKING_POLICY - Configuration for chunking strategies (see ChunkingPolicySchema)

docs.title: Event Hooks
docs.text: The AI Core module emits events via the eventbus for memory lifecycle events: - checkpoint-create - When a checkpoint is created - checkpoint-save - When a checkpoint is saved - memory-store-put - When an item is stored in long-term memory - memory-store-get - When an item is retrieved from long-term memory

docs.title: MSFLib Auth Module
docs.text: The Auth module provides authentication, token lifecycle, and reusable FastAPI dependency factories for authorization.

docs.title: What This Module Provides
docs.text:
• Login and access token issuance
  • Token revocation (logout)
  • Password recovery and reset flows
  • Optional Google OAuth login and callback
  • Account-level and workspace-level authorization dependency factories

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
For Pydantic v2 (recommended):

[tool.poetry.dependencies]
msflib = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "core", rev = "dev" }
msflib-auth = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "modules/auth", rev = "dev" }

For Pydantic v1 (legacy):

[tool.poetry.dependencies]
pydantic = "^1.10"
pydantic-settings = "^1.10"

msflib = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "core", rev = "core-v0.1.1" }
msflib-auth = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "modules/auth", rev = "auth-v0.1.1" }

See Pydantic Version Compatibility for migration guidance.

docs.title: 1) Build dependencies once
docs.text:
from msflib.auth.deps import get_account_dependencies, get_user_dependencies
from msflib.auth.resolvers import PathParameterResolver

account_deps = get_account_dependencies(
    AccountModel=Account,
    oauth_token_url="/api/v1/auth/login",
    secret_key=settings.SECRET_KEY,
    session_dep=get_session,
    keystore_dep=get_keystore,
)

user_deps = get_user_dependencies(
    UserModel=WorkspaceUser,
    WorkspaceModel=Workspace,
    session_dep=get_session,
    account_dependencies=account_deps,
    workspace_resolver=PathParameterResolver(),
)

docs.title: 2) Mount auth routes
docs.text:
from fastapi import FastAPI
from msflib.auth.router import router as auth_router

app = FastAPI()
app.include_router(
    auth_router(
        get_session=get_session,
        get_keystore=get_keystore,
        get_current_account=account_deps.get_current_account,
        account_type=Account,
        account_read_type=AccountRead,
        settings=settings,
        prefix="/auth",
    )
)

docs.title: API Surface (/auth)
docs.text:
• POST /login
  • GET /google/login (when enabled)
  • POST /google/callback (when enabled)
  • POST /password-recovery
  • POST /verify-token
  • POST /reset-password
  • DELETE /logout

docs.title: Google Callback Auth Payload
docs.text:
The auth router supports passing frontend-provided payload data during Google OAuth completion.

Use auth_payload_type when creating the router to inject a Pydantic model for validation:

from pydantic import BaseModel


class GoogleAuthPayload(BaseModel):
    workspace_id: str

docs.title: Dependencies (msflib.auth.deps)
docs.text:
The module provides two main dependency factories:

  1. get_account_dependencies - Creates reusable dependencies for account authentication & authorization:
  2. get_current_account - Requires a valid, non-revoked token
  3. get_current_account_or_none - Same but returns None for unauthenticated requests
  4. get_current_active_account - Additionally validates account status
  5. get_current_active_superuser - Additionally validates role == "root"

  6. RoleCheck - Callable class for role-based guards

  7. get_user_dependencies - Creates reusable dependencies for workspace+user identity & authorization:

  8. get_current_workspace - Resolves the active workspace for an authenticated request
  9. get_current_workspace_anonymous - Resolves workspace without authentication
  10. get_current_user - Resolves the authenticated account's membership in the active workspace
  11. get_current_active_user - Additionally validates user status
  12. WorkspaceRoleCheck - Callable class for workspace role guards

docs.title: Resolvers (msflib.auth.resolvers)
docs.text: Workspace resolution strategies: - HttpHeaderResolver - Resolves workspace from HTTP headers - PathParameterResolver - Resolves workspace from path parameters - WorkspaceResolver - Base class for custom resolvers

docs.title: Router (msflib.auth.router)
docs.text: Provides the authentication endpoints router that can be mounted in a FastAPI application.

docs.title: Basic Account Authentication
docs.text:
from fastapi import Depends
from msflib.auth.deps import get_account_dependencies

account_deps = get_account_dependencies(
    AccountModel=Account,
    oauth_token_url="/auth/login",
    secret_key=settings.SECRET_KEY,
    session_dep=get_session,
    keystore_dep=get_keystore,
)

@app.get("/protected")
def protected_route(
    current_account: Account = Depends(account_deps.get_current_account)
):
    return {"message": f"Hello {current_account.email}"}

docs.title: Workspace-User Authorization
docs.text:
from fastapi import Depends
from msflib.auth.deps import get_user_dependencies
from msflib.auth.resolvers import PathParameterResolver

user_deps = get_user_dependencies(
    UserModel=WorkspaceUser,
    WorkspaceModel=Workspace,
    session_dep=get_session,
    account_dependencies=account_deps,
    workspace_resolver=PathParameterResolver(),
)

@app.get("/ws/{workspace_id}/data")
def workspace_data(
    current_user: WorkspaceUser = Depends(user_deps.get_current_user),
    current_workspace: Workspace = Depends(user_deps.get_current_workspace)
):
    return {"workspace": current_workspace.name, "user": current_user.email}

docs.title: Role-Based Access Control
docs.text:
from fastapi import Depends
from msflib.auth.deps import get_account_dependencies

account_deps = get_account_dependencies(
    AccountModel=Account,
    oauth_token_url="/auth/login",
    secret_key=settings.SECRET_KEY,
    session_dep=get_session,
    keystore_dep=get_keystore,
)

@app.get("/admin")
def admin_only(
    _: bool = Depends(account_deps.RoleCheck(["root", "admin"]))
):
    return {"message": "Admin access granted"}

docs.title: MSFLib Payments Module
docs.text: The Payments module is integral to handling various aspects of payment processing, including initiation, verification through gateways, and queue-driven post-payment processing.

docs.title: What This Module Provides
docs.text:
• Unified PaymentProcessor: Supports integration with multiple payment gateways such as Stripe and Paystack.
  • Persistence: Manages the state of payments and payment-queue information.
  • Verification Endpoints: Ensures proper payment confirmation and handling.
  • Event Emission: Enables downstream processing once payment events occur.

docs.title: For Pydantic v2 (recommended)
docs.text:
Add the following to your pyproject.toml:

[tool.poetry.dependencies]
msflib = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "core", rev = "dev" }
msflib-payments = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "modules/payments", rev = "dev" }

docs.title: For Pydantic v1 (legacy)
docs.text:
[tool.poetry.dependencies]
pydantic = "^1.10"
pydantic-settings = "^1.10"

msflib = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "core", rev = "core-v0.1.1" }
msflib-payments = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "modules/payments", rev = "payments-v0.1.0" }

Refer to Pydantic Version Compatibility for migration guidance.

docs.title: 1) Mount Routes
docs.text:
To integrate the payments router into a FastAPI application:

from fastapi import FastAPI
from msflib.payments.router import router as payments_router

app = FastAPI()
app.include_router(
    payments_router(
        get_session=get_session,
        get_current_account=get_current_account,
        settings=settings,
        prefix="/payments",
    )
)

docs.title: 2) Initiate Payments
docs.text:
Trigger payment processing within your business logic:

from msflib.payments.models import PaymentData
from msflib.payments.service.processor import process_payment

payment = await process_payment(
    session=session,
    payment_data=PaymentData(
        amount=5000,
        description="Subscription",

    ),
    account=current_account,
    settings=settings,

)

docs.title: MSFLib FastAPI Project - Documentation Overview
docs.text: This repository contains a collection of reusable modules for building FastAPI applications with MSFLib. Each module provides specific functionality that can be integrated into a FastAPI project.

docs.title: Modules
docs.text:
• Account - Account and profile management
  • AI Core - Infrastructure for AI features (LLMs, embeddings, vector stores, etc.)
  • Auth - Authentication and authorization
  • Drivelink - File storage and management
  • Notifications - Notification services
  • Payments - Payment processing

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: Each module can be installed independently via Git. Refer to the individual module documentation for installation and usage instructions.

docs.title: Common Patterns
docs.text: Many modules follow similar patterns for integration: - Routers are provided for FastAPI inclusion - Settings are configured via Pydantic settings - Dependency injection helpers are provided for FastAPI endpoints

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: See the individual module READMEs for contribution guidelines.

docs.title: MSFLib WorkspaceConfig Module
docs.text: The MSFLib WorkspaceConfig module provides a foundational framework for building reusable modules for projects using FastAPI and MSFLib. It delivers scoped configuration persistence, catering to tenant, workspace, and user-level configurations, with predictable override behaviors.

docs.title: Key Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Scoped Configuration: Manages and persists configurations across various scopes like tenant, workspace, and user, ensuring precise and predictable configuration use.
  • Installation: Support for two Pydantic versions is provided. Installation is done via Poetry by fetching the msflib and msflib-workspace_config from a Git repository.
  • Request Override Allowlist: This feature prevents unauthorized configuration changes by allowing modules to define a request_override_allowlist. This ensures only safe modifications can be done via per-request overrides.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
To integrate this module in a FastAPI application, import workspace_config_router and include it in your FastAPI app configuration:

from fastapi import FastAPI
from msflib.workspace_config.router import router as workspace_config_router

app = FastAPI()
app.include_router(
    workspace_config_router(
        get_session=get_session,
        settings=settings,
        prefix="/workspace_config",
        tags=["workspace_config"],
    )
)

The module uses:

settings.scope("WORKSPACE_CONFIG")

To read module settings.

docs.title: Tiered Configuration Role
docs.text: The module contributes to a broader configuration management responsibility: - Core Module: Acts as the resolver and precedence engine. - WorkspaceConfig Module: Provides management APIs for scoped persistence. - Consuming Modules/Applications: Utilize the resolved configurations for their domain-specific operational needs.

docs.title: Request Override Handling
docs.text: ScopedConfigService within the module processes request-specific configuration override actions, respecting the defined allowlist to prevent unsafe alterations.

docs.title: Workspaces Module
docs.text: The Workspaces module is responsible for managing the lifecycle of workspaces and utilities related to workspace membership. It provides several key capabilities as part of its API offerings.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Workspace CRUD Endpoints: These endpoints not only allow creating, reading, updating, and deleting workspaces but also include ownership checks to manage and verify access control effectively.
  • Automatic Owner Membership: Upon the creation of a workspace, the module automatically handles the creation of memberships for owners, ensuring immediate access and control assignment.
  • Workspace Discovery: An endpoint exists to assist in discovering available workspaces, facilitating easier navigation and selection for users.
  • Logo Management: Offers functionality for uploading workspace logos and cleaning up any previous logos efficiently to maintain workspace branding consistency.
  • Profile Routing: Integrates with the workspace profile router using a defined path pattern (/{workspace_slug}/profiles), allowing profiles to be associated with specific workspace contexts.

docs.title: For Pydantic v2 (Recommended)
docs.text:
To use the Workspaces module with Pydantic v2, include the following dependencies in your pyproject.toml file:

[tool.poetry.dependencies]
msflib = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "core", rev = "dev" }
msflib-account = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "modules/account", rev = "dev" }
msflib-workspaces = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "modules/workspaces", rev = "dev" }

docs.title: For Pydantic v1 (Legacy)
docs.text:
For legacy support with Pydantic v1, use the following dependencies:

[tool.poetry.dependencies]
pydantic = "^1.10"
pydantic-settings = "^1.10"
msflib = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "core", rev = "core-v0.1.1" }
msflib-account = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "modules/account", rev = "account-v0.1.0" }
msflib-workspaces = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "modules/workspaces", rev = "workspaces-v0.1.1" }

Refer to the Pydantic Version Compatibility section for guidance on migrating between Pydantic versions.

docs.title: 1. Mount Workspace Routes
docs.text:
Integrate workspace routes into a FastAPI application by including the workspace router:

from fastapi import FastAPI
from msflib.workspaces.router import router as workspaces_router

app = FastAPI()
app.include_router(
    workspaces_router(
        get_session=get_session,
        get_current_account=get_current_account,
        get_current_account_or_none=get_current_account_or_none,
        role_check=role_check,
        settings=settings,
        prefix="/workspaces",
    )
)

docs.title: 1b. Override Workspace Form Processors
docs.text:
The module allows customization of data processing logic by providing default implementations that can be overridden. For instance, modifying the workspace creation handler:

from fastapi import Form
from typing import Optional
from msflib.workspaces import get_workspace_form_dependencies
from msflib.workspaces.models import WorkspaceCreate, WorkspaceUpdate

form_deps = get_workspace_form_dependencies(
    workspace_create_type=WorkspaceCreate,
    workspace_update_type=WorkspaceUpdate,
)

original_get_workspace_create = form_deps.get_workspace_create

def custom_get_workspace_create(
    name: str = Form(...),
    description: str = Form(...),
    status: str = Form("open"),
    data: str = Form(default="{}"),
    settings: Optional[str] = Form(default=None),
):
    payload = original_get_workspace_create(
        name=name,
        description=description,
        status=status,
        data=data,
        settings=settings,
    )
    payload.name = f"tenant-{payload.name}"
    return payload

This setup allows developers to wrap or replace existing form processors, thereby injecting custom logic where necessary.
